newsitem.title: USA: Chicago teachers in trouble for showing videos to kids.
newsitem.headline: Chicago teachers in trouble for showing videos to kids.

text.p: Classroom showings of the movies "Scream" and "The Long Kiss Goodnight" to middle school students at a Chicago school last week may result in teachers being disciplined, school authorities said Monday.
A teacher at an elementary school was also facing dismissal for permitting students under 10 years old to view a video of the film "Striptease."

As many as 200 eighth-graders at John Marshall Middle school were allowed to view Wes Craven's frightening "Scream" on video, a "splatter" film about a serial killer attacking teenagers, as well as adult-themed movies such as "Sixteen Candles," "Cable Guy" and "The Long Kiss Goodnight."

Chicago school board spokeswoman Blondean Davis said the school's principal gave the rationale that "the (14-year-old) students were studying film, literary and media materials in preparation for writing their own stories.
"Absolutely, it's a waste of time," Davis said, adding that four teachers and the principal may be disciplined.

In a seperate incident, a 55-year-old computer classroom teacher faces dismissal for permitting students as young as nine to rummage through his bag of videos and watch "Striptease," which features a partially clad character played by Demi Moore, last week at Smyth Elementary school.
"The (school) board is seeking his dismissal," school spokeswoman Tabrina Davis said. The teacher has been transferred to a non-teaching position pending a hearing.
The Chicago Sun-Times reported that a parent happened to walk by the unsupervised classroom at a point in the film where Moore's character was stripping.
Chicago schools chief Paul Vallas criticised the teachers involved and insisted that the city's public school system was geared toward "wall-to-wall instruction."
